intended_object: Given a Vitali family v for μ and a measure ν ≪ μ, the same family of sets viewed as a Vitali family for ν. This is the standard fact that a Vitali relation for μ is also one for any ν absolutely continuous with respect to μ. Inferred from the docstring and name.
explanation: The definition copies every field of `v` unchanged: `setsAt`, measurability, nonempty interiors and `nontrivial`. None of these fields depends on the measure. Only the covering property mentions the measure. For that field, the definition takes the disjoint subfamily that `v` produces for μ. The set it leaves uncovered has μ-measure zero, so by `hν : ν ≪ μ` it also has ν-measure zero. This is exactly the intended transfer: the same family of sets, now a Vitali family for ν. The setting matches that of `VitaliFamily` itself (a pseudometric space with a measure), and absolute continuity is exactly the hypothesis the argument needs. So the definition is neither too narrow nor wrong. Mathlib has no other declaration doing this transfer.
